ai.title: Fix hang after terminal command in client.ts
ai.summary: Refactored `stopResponse` in `npm-app/src/client.ts` to call `unsubscribeComplete()` immediately alongside `unsubscribeChunks()`. Removed conditional `promptId` check that previously delayed `unsubscribeComplete()`. Ensures subscription cleanup occurs reliably to prevent hanging after terminal command execution.

eli5.text: When you ran a command in the terminal, the app could sometimes freeze and stop responding. The app now cleans up its background work immediately after you run a command, so it won't get stuck waiting and will respond normally afterward. This affects anyone using the terminal feature and should already be live.

ai.title: Version 1.0.179 fixes client unsubscribe logic
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.179. `npm-app/src/client.ts` adjusts `unsubscribeComplete()` calls in `stopResponse` and prompt ID mismatch handling, moving the call from a TODO comment to active code in one branch and removing it from another. This ensures proper resource cleanup during stream termination. Scope limited to `npm-app` package.

eli5.text: When you stop an assistant response mid-stream, the system now correctly cleans up background connections instead of leaving them open or closing the wrong ones. Previously the cleanup step was disabled in one important situation and incorrectly active in another, which could cause the app to hang or waste resources. If you watched the app during a stop, you'd no longer see it freeze after a command finishes or leave lingering streams when a new prompt arrives. The fix is live today in the version you install now.

ai.title: Upgrade @anthropic-ai/sdk to 0.39.0
ai.summary: Bumped @anthropic-ai/sdk from ^0.36.3 to ^0.39.0 in backend/package.json. Internal dependency update.

eli5.text: The system that powers the assistant behind the scenes now uses a newer version of the software library that connects to Anthropic's models. The developers bumped the version in the project's dependency list, swapping out the old library version for a newer one that includes updates and bug fixes from Anthropic. If you looked under the hood, you'd see the version number in the project's package file changed from 0.36.3 to 0.39.0. For most people, this won't change anything you can see or do, but it helps keep the system running smoothly behind the scenes.

ai.title: Standardize lazy edit placeholder comments
ai.summary: Prompts in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/tools.ts` now enforce language-specific comment syntax (e.g., `// ... existing code ...`) for lazy edits instead of bare ellipses. `backend/src/process-file-block.ts` updated to explicitly reject these markers during apply-model processing. `common/src/util/string.ts` adds detection for the standardized `... existing code ...` pattern in `hasLazyEdit`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to edit a file, it now writes placeholder comments that match the programming language being used. Instead of a generic "... existing code...", it uses the correct comment style for that language, such as "//... existing code..." for JavaScript, "#... existing code..." for Python, or "<!--... existing code... -->" for HTML. This helps the file-editing system better recognize where your changes are, since it looks for these language-specific comment patterns. The change is live now and affects any edit suggestion the assistant makes to a file.

ai.title: Saxy ignores unclosed tags
ai.summary: Saxy parser no longer throws Error on unclosed tags. Node.tagClose case now returns silently instead of invoking callback with error. Affects common/src/util/saxy.ts.

eli5.text: When you open a document and forget to close a section (like leaving a '<title>' tag open), the app used to stop and show an error. Now it quietly ignores that mistake and keeps going instead of interrupting you. You might not notice anything different unless you were relying on that error message to catch typos in hand-written files. The fix lives in the app's text-reading tool and is active today.

ai.title: Drop checkout from storeFileState in file-manager
ai.summary: Removed redundant `checkout` call from `storeFileState` in `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts` and refactored `restoreFileState` to eliminate `resetDone` flag. Internal logic now relies on `git reset --hard` or isomorphic-git `checkout` + `resetIndex` only during restore, not store. Renamed `stageFiles` to `gitAddAll` and added JSDoc comments.

eli5.text: When the assistant saves a snapshot of your project's files, it no longer switches your working files to that snapshot at the same time, which speeds up and simplifies the save step. When the assistant later needs to bring your files back to a previously saved snapshot, it still performs the full switch then. If you were reviewing the save-and-switch behavior step by step, you would now see the switch happen only during restoration, not during storage.

ai.title: Fix terminal hang for commands without output
ai.summary: Corrects a hang in `runCommandPty` within `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` when commands produce no output. The prompt identifier trimming logic now checks `(commandOutput + pendingOutput).trim() === ''` instead of just `commandOutput.trim() === ''`. This ensures the condition evaluates correctly against accumulated data, preventing the process from stalling.

eli5.text: When the assistant ran a command that produced no output, the terminal could freeze and stop responding. Now the program waits to look at all the text it has gathered so far before deciding the command is done, so commands that simply return no result will complete instead of hanging. You would notice the terminal finishing promptly instead of stalling on such commands. It is live today.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.180
ai.summary: Package version incremented from 1.0.179 to 1.0.180 in `npm-app/package.json`. This is a standard release preparation step for the `codebuff` CLI package. No functional code changes or dependency updates accompany this revision.

eli5.text: Your AI coding helper got a routine packaging update, like a refreshed install file that helps keep your setup current. This update is already live today. It also bundles several small fixes you'll get: the assistant no longer freezes when running commands that produce no output, and it handles a wider variety of code formatting edge cases more smoothly. If you update the tool now, the most noticeable difference is that terminal commands are less likely to hang waiting for output that never arrives.
